deities: Rishi Ved Vyas (meditation shrine; no conventional murti)

history.summary: Vyas Gufa is an ancient cave at the foot of the new Bilaspur township on the left (east) bank of the Satluj river (now on the shores of Gobind Sagar), where Rishi Ved Vyas — compiler of the Mahabharata and the Puranas — is believed to have meditated for years. The origin of the town's name, Vyaspur (now Bilaspur, a distorted form of Vyas-pur), is traditionally derived from this cave. The ancient Lakshmi Narayan and Radheyshyam temples along with the Vyas Gufa escaped submersion when the Bhakra reservoir filled. A folk account says the cave tunnels ~4-5 km through the mountain to a 'Vyas gupha' cave at Markand Makri (site of seq 1570, Markandeya Ji Temple). Coordinates are for Diara Sector, Bilaspur new township — approximate for the cave, which sits at the township's foot by the river (verify).

name: Vyas Gufa (Vyas Cave)
town_description: Bilaspur is a historic town and the district headquarters of Bilaspur district in Himachal Pradesh, situated on the banks of the Satluj river and the Govind Sagar reservoir created by the Bhakra Dam. The old town was submerged when the dam was built in the 1960s and a new township was established on higher ground. It is an important pilgrimage corridor, home to the Naina Devi temple (51 Shakti Peethas) nearby.
